metadata.title: How Do You Contain an AI Agent That Misbehaves?
metadata.note: STEM/AI topic-of-interest video, a direct follow-on to the Agent Orchestration video's closing lesson ('more autonomy needs more oversight'). Covers unexpected/aggressive autonomous-agent behavior in grounded, practical terms — not speculative sci-fi framing. Real failure modes: literal/narrow goal pursuit producing unintended actions, scope creep beyond intended permissions, repeated/looping failed actions, unanticipated tool use. Practical containment: scoped permissions, sandboxing, action logging, human checkpoints before high-stakes or irreversible actions, and a circuit breaker to halt on deviation. Honest caveat: containment adds friction and no system is perfectly safe — the goal is reducing risk and preserving visibility, not eliminating all possibility of unexpected behavior. Built using the same proven pattern set as prior videos: folderLabel set explicitly on ClaudeComposerAsk beats (@HumanitariansAI), OutroCTA used instead of ClaudeTitleOutro, BLUF lines kept short to avoid edge-bleed, no stale sparse_by_design flags except the legitimate BrutalistHesitantWriter typing-beat exemption.
